title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Elementary set-up, apparently preparing the CM-field / CM-motive material in the 'Galois theory of motives' notes.

(1) Definitions. Let K/Q be an algebraic extension (the word 'algébrique' replaces a crossed-out 'de degré [fini]'). K is totally real if σ(K) ⊂ R for every Q-embedding σ: K → C. An element x ∈ K is totally real (resp. totally >0, resp. totally ≥0) if σ(x) is real (resp. >0, resp. ≥0) for all such σ. 'Totally (or purely) imaginary' is left as '....'.

(2) Scholium.
- x is totally real iff the subfield Q(x) is totally real.
- x is totally ≥0 iff x = 0 or x is totally >0.
- The totally ≥0 elements are the nonnegative elements of a (partial) order on K, written x tot. ≥ y.
- If K is generated by subfields K_α (resp. by elements x_α), K is totally real iff all K_α (resp. all x_α) are.
- Hence every K has a largest totally real subfield, the 'totally real closure of Q in K'.

(3) Galois-theoretic description. Fix Q̄ ⊂ C, π = Gal(Q̄/Q), and τ ∈ π complex conjugation, with τ² = 1. The subgroup π' fixing Q^tr (the totally real closure of Q in Q̄, written 𝕂) is the closed normal subgroup generated by τ, i.e. by the conjugates τ_σ = στσ⁻¹. Indeed, λ is totally real iff it is fixed by every στσ⁻¹.

(4) Abelianization. Let A be the maximal abelian extension of 𝕂, with Gal(A/𝕂) = H = π'/(π',π'). The page ends here. The next page draws the conclusion: H is topologically generated by the G-conjugates of the image of τ, all involutions, so the abelian group H is killed by 2. Equivalently, every abelian extension of Q^tr is a compositum of quadratic extensions.

(5) Next page. A nontrivial abelian L/𝕂 that is Galois over Q has all conjugates of τ coinciding on it iff it is quadratic and Galois over Q iff it is a totally imaginary quadratic extension. Such L is unique, namely L = Q^tr(√−1) = Q^cm, the maximal CM field.

Purpose: to set up Q^tr and Q^cm and the Galois groups that later govern CM motives (Serre group / Taniyama-type groups).
errors: Transcription/reading: 'il faut et il suffit qu'il soit réel ou tot >0' should read 'nul ou tot >0'. As transcribed, the statement would be false.

'Relation d'ordre' is only a partial order, which is correct but unstated. Also, 'K engendré par des x_α ⇒ K tot. réel ssi les x_α le sont' is fine for algebraic K because a compositum of totally real fields is totally real.

(Next page) 'G = π/π' ... qui est commutatif ... annulé par 2' conflates G with H. It is H = π'^ab, not G = Gal(Q^tr/Q), that is commutative, generated by the G-conjugates of τ̇, and killed by 2. G is far from abelian.

ideas.what: Totally real / totally positive elements and fields, the partial order 'tot. ≥', and the maximal totally real subfield
ideas.modern_name: totally real fields, totally positive elements

ideas.what: Gal(Q̄/Q^tr) is the closed normal subgroup generated by complex conjugation
ideas.modern_name: Q^tr as fixed field of the conjugates of complex conjugation

ideas.what: Abelianization of Gal(Q̄/Q^tr) is killed by 2 (it is generated by involutions); every abelian extension of Q^tr has exponent 2
ideas.modern_name: consequence of Gal(Q̄/Q^tr) being generated by involutions; refined by Fried–Haran–Völklein's description of Gal(Q^tr) as a free product of Z/2's

ideas.what: Unique quadratic extension of Q^tr Galois over Q on which all conjugates of τ agree: Q^cm = Q^tr(i)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shimura–Taniyama / Weil; used by Serre (Serre group, 1968) and Deligne (Taniyama group)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly records that Gal(Q̄/Q^tr) is normally generated by complex conjugation, so its abelianization has exponent 2. This is in the context of a motivic Galois theory. It is an early, motivic-context appearance of the Q^tr / Q^cm framework later formalized via the Serre and Taniyama groups. The mathematics itself is elementary and known.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only historical: it documents Grothendieck preparing CM-motive Galois groups (Q^cm, Serre group). It may predate or parallel Serre's 1968 treatment, depending on the uncertain dating (1965 to c.1977).

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary, correct field theory (totally real fields, Q^tr, Q^cm). The only point of interest is historical context within the motivic Galois notes, and the dating is uncertain.
transcription_corrections: 'il suffit qu'il soit réel ou tot >0' → 'il suffit qu'il soit nul ou tot >0'
'Considérons la plus grande extension abélienne A de K' — here K is the blackboard 𝕂 = totally real closure of Q in Q̄ (Q^tr), not the arbitrary K of the definition
'Alors le ss-groupe π' ... → ss-groupe invariant fermé engendré par τ' — the arrow is the author's shorthand for 'est le'
